_why: The device server this app carries inside itself.
ForgeFX is a separate project (MIT, sKuhLight) and we ship a copy of it in the
installer. Two consequences follow, and this file is both of them.
First, we vendor from our own private mirrors rather than from upstream. What
goes inside something we sign should not depend on another account's repository
still being there, still being public, and still having the history it had last
week. `upstream` records where each mirror came from, because provenance is the
thing a copy loses first.
Second, the pin is the commit. The mirrors carry every branch and the whole
history but no tags, so `tag` is a label for people and `commit` is what
scripts/vendor-forgefx.mjs actually asks GitHub for. That is stricter than
cloning a tag and checking it afterwards: there is no window in which the wrong
code is on disk. Where a remote does have the tag, the script still checks it
points here.
forgefx-midi is the preset codec ForgeFX depends on. Its ref is not ours to
choose: ForgeFX pins its own sibling in stack.lock.json for exactly the tag
builds we are copying, so the script cross-checks the tag below against that
file and refuses to build a pair upstream never released together.
The pin is a branch of the mirror rather than a plain upstream commit. Naming
the preset or a scene was refused by the host's own remoteAllowed() — absent
from the writes it permits and absent from the list of things it says are
never remotely reachable, which reads as an oversight rather than a boundary.
It is an edit-buffer write like every other one allowed there, and committing
to a slot is still refused, so it cannot overwrite anything on the unit.
Kept on a branch so the mirror's main stays a clean copy of upstream: the next
upstream release is a rebase of one commit rather than a merge conflict.
The branch now also carries host addressing. The remote channel is per
ACCOUNT, so a request is not sent to a host -- it is shouted, and every host
signed into that account answers it. With two Macs that meant a read was
answered twice and a WRITE WAS CARRIED OUT TWICE, on two different units. The
host now honours an optional `host` field naming the Mac a request is meant
for, and stays silent on anything addressed elsewhere. Absent on every request
from a client that has only ever seen one host, so it is inert until there are
two.
And tuner readings now cross the relay. They were dropped with the meter and
CPU cadence, which was right for those -- they run continuously for any
subscribed client -- and wrong for the tuner, whose poll exists only while
somebody has it open. Dropping it broke the one place a remote tuner is worth
anything: tuning from a phone away from the Mac. Throttled to one reading
every 80 ms so a future poll cadence cannot flood the relay.

The branch moved again, and for a fault a player hit twice: "PRESET_DUMP_HEADER: expected func 0x77 at offset 0, got 0x78" on switching presets. The server decided a preset dump had arrived by checking for chunks and a terminator and taking the header on trust, so a dump whose HEADER went missing was handed to the codec instead of being re-read by the retry that was already there. The fix sits on top of the three patches above rather than on upstream main, which does not carry them — re-pinning to main would have taken renaming, host addressing and the remote tuner away with it.
